title.narrative: Strengthening access to essential Health and Nutrition services for drought-affected populations in Rural Bossaso district.

description.narrative: ltpgtISDP proposes a 12-month integrated health and nutrition program in Bossaso to strengthen the health and nutrition outcomes of drought-affected populations in rural areas through enhanced delivery and utilization of essential services. The program will focus on maternal, infant, and young child care, integrated disease prevention, and community-based nutrition, combining life-saving interventions with primary health care to reduce preventable morbidity and mortality while building resilient communities. Services will be delivered across 14 health and nutrition sites, ensuring equitable access through fixed and outreach services. The 14 sites include 2 health facilities with BEmONC services, 3 health facilities without BEmONC services, 4 PHU Plus, 1 SC, and 4 outreach sites supported by 1 outreach team.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThrough targeted capacity building, 82 health and nutrition programming staff, including volunteers, will be trained on emergency obstetric care, IMNCI, PMCI, IMAM, MCH, immunization, MPHSS, and effective health data management. CHWs, 14, will provide community-level messaging, counseling, and follow-up, ensuring early detection, timely referral, and continuity of care. Health and nutrition services will be integrated to ensure effective inter-referrals between ANC, PNC, OPD, SC/OTP/TSFP, and mental health services. ISDP will provide services targeting 60,000 outpatient consultations, antenatal care for over 12,000 women, 2,250 safe deliveries, 120 cesarean sections, measles vaccination for 10,110 children, DPT for 7077 children and psychosocial support for 2,200 individuals. Mental health treatment will reach 72 cases through integrated facility and outreach-based services.ltbrgtNutrition interventions will include OTP, TSFP, MUAC screening, and MIYCN. ISDP will treat and rehabilitate 240 children with complicated SAM at the Bosaso Stabilization Centre, 1,900 children with uncomplicated SAM, and 6,350 children and 6,800 PLW with MAM across fixed and outreach sites. Caregivers will receive targeted counseling and support through 14 MTMSG and 42 sessions to promote Kobciye Shurbad approach. Vitamin A supplementation will target 6,200, while routine deworming will reach 5,000 children. Supplies including RUSF, RUTF, CSB++, F100, F75, and routine medications will be provided through the MoH, UNICEF, WFP, and WHO, with ISDP procuring buffer stock to ensure uninterrupted treatment and service delivery. The program will aim for 50% of caregivers to demonstrate improved knowledge and adoption of recommended feeding and care practices.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtISDP will integrate protection, gender, and accountability across all activities, training 82 staff and volunteers on PSEA, child protection, GBV, AAP, and PDAD. 24 community engagement sessions will ensure inclusion and participation of vulnerable groups. ISDP will closely coordinate with FSL, WASH, and protection partners, as well as WFP, UNICEF, and WHO, to complement interventions and ensure uninterrupted service delivery. The program will use standardized MoH and Health and Nutrition Cluster tools integrated into ISDP’s ME system and indicator tracking table for systematic tracking, data collection, analysis, and adaptive management. Data will be reported using Kobo Toolbox, DHIS2, and ONA, capturing age, gender, and diversity factors. The exit strategy will transition key activities to MoH, with CHWs and MTMSGs continuing routine service delivery. Community protection and engagement structures will remain active, and trainings, including Family MUAC, IYCF, and the Kobciye Shurbad approach, will foster lasting behavior change. Procurement and supply management will reduce stock-outs and ensure availability of medicines, nutrition commodities, and IEC materials. ISDP will ensure interventions remain accessible, culturally appropriate, and responsive to women, children, and vulnerable populations, while continuous monitoring will guide adaptive management and inform future programming.ltbrgtlt/pgt
